conflicts.fact: What the Lesson 1 sorting groups did with the mosquito and chicken, which Lesson 4 refers back to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 claims that in the first lesson one group put the mosquito and the chicken together because both can fly. Lesson 1 only lists criteria such as habitat, colour, size, usefulness and green/mobile, and never records this grouping. The sorting is only a recalled example, so it is a minor inconsistency.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson's model/Kingdom content is referenced when the five kingdoms are introduced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the model cannot yet explain how organisms are placed into the Five Kingdoms and asks 'How many Kingdoms are there?'. Lesson 4 says the model already shows a 'Kingdom-level split into groups is useful', though no earlier lesson built that. Lesson 6 ends with the question 'Can organisms with similar features be grouped into larger categories?', which the hierarchy lessons 3-4 already answered.

conflicts.fact: Sequence of the lessons on hierarchy versus binomial naming and kingdoms
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 ends by saying we still need to learn how organisms are named with Genus and species, while Lesson 4 ends by asking how to give a species a unique name. Lesson 6 ends by asking whether similar organisms can be grouped into larger categories, and Lesson 7 is on kingdoms, so the next-lesson questions repeat or regress to ideas already covered in lessons 3-4.
